questions.q: What evidence confirms the root cause of the AP aging mismatch?
options: A missing supplier bank account
A duplicate supplier record for Meridian
Two separate entries for the same PO in account 2150 — the unreversed December GRNI journal and January's validated invoice, both $18,400.00
An invoice entered to the wrong business unit
questions.explain: Checking account 2150 reveals both JE-GRNI-1231 and the accounting from INV-MER-88341's validation, confirming the accrual never reversed before the real invoice posted.

questions.q: What technique immediately reveals the AR problem on Harborview's account?
options: Reviewing the total AR control account balance only
Pulling Harborview's AR aging detail by invoice instead of by total account balance
Checking the customer's credit limit
Reviewing the bank reconciliation for January
questions.explain: Looking at invoice-level detail shows one invoice falsely overdue and another falsely overpaid, which a total-balance view would never reveal.

questions.q: How is FA-10452's depreciation root cause confirmed?
options: By rerunning the depreciation program with a different book
By contacting the equipment manufacturer directly
By reviewing Harborview's AR aging report
By comparing the asset record's category and cost center against the capital approval paperwork for a CNC lathe
questions.explain: Cross-checking FA-10452's recorded category and cost center against the actual capital approval paperwork confirms it should be Manufacturing Equipment in Fabrication, not Office Equipment in Assembly.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what should happen before any correction is made to these three items?
options: The root cause should be confirmed with actual evidence — the journal, the receipt application history, or the asset record — before touching anything
Corrections should be made immediately upon suspicion to save time
The CFO must personally approve each investigation step
The period must be closed before any investigation begins
questions.explain: The lesson emphasizes confirming root causes with real evidence before proposing or making any correction, which is left to lesson 21.

questions.q: Does this lesson actually correct any of the three problems it investigates?
options: Yes, all three are corrected and reconciled by the end of this lesson
No — this lesson only confirms root causes; corrections happen in lesson 21
Only the AP accrual is corrected here
Only the Harborview receipt is corrected here
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly states nothing is corrected yet — all three root causes are confirmed with evidence, and fixing them is reserved for lesson 21.
